Step 3: left changed only the bottom-right active 3 on the 11-bar: it expanded/moved one cell left (now 2 columns wide across the bottom 2 rows). This suggests left may not affect the main board while 3 is selected, or the bottom bar is a move/selection indicator.

Step 7: right also produced no obvious main-board change beyond extending the bottom 3 indicator. This strengthens the idea that many actions merely append to a history/selection bar once 3 is active. Next informative probe: try select again to see if it cycles the active piece/color or confirms another state.
Step 8: second select caused a large state change. The upper-left part of the top 5 block turned into a 3 block (rows ~3-8, cols ~9-14), while the lower-left attached 3 and its nearby 1 disappeared. Next probe: try down, since up was previously the only direction that caused a substantive transfer-like change and the active 3 is now on the top anchor.

Step 12: up from the lower-left 4+8 anchor produced another substantive change: the lower-left became 4+8+1 (rows ~33-38, cols ~3-20), while the top 3+5 anchor and upper-left 8+1 stayed unchanged. This again fits the idea that an anchor may have one meaningful directional action before select cycles the active state. Next informative probe: select again.
Step 13: select caused another major state change: the top anchor became 3+8+5 (rows ~3-8, cols ~9-32), while the lower-left 4+8+1 collapsed back to just 4 and upper-left 8+1 stayed. Hypothesis: select may promote/transfer an attached block from a lower anchor up into the top anchor.

Step 2: select caused a visible change near the right end of the bottom 11-bar; hypothesis: select activates/cycles a color/piece.
Step 3-4: left mainly expanded/moved the bottom-right 3 on the 11-bar. Likely history/progress, not main movement.
Step 5: first strong board change came from up: upper-left 8/1 relation changed while lower-left gained a 1.
Step 6-10: many actions after selecting 3 mostly extended the bottom 3 indicator; meaningful changes tended to happen once per anchor, then stall.
Step 11-12: select moved attention to the lower-left anchor (4 next to 8), and up transformed it to 4+8+1.
Step 13-14: select promoted 8 into the top anchor (top became 3+8+5), and down redistributed that promoted state back into lower-left / upper-left structures.
Step 15-18: lower-left was gradually reduced from 4+8+1 toward pure 4; up on pure 4 converted it to pure 1.
Step 19-20: select promoted 1 into the top anchor (top 3+8+1+5), then promoted/cycled 4 into the top anchor (top 3+8+1+4).

Step 35-47: main board still appeared stable while the bottom bar transition from 11 to 3 kept creeping left.
Step 48-50 insight: one more right appears to overfill the bar and reset progress back near an early selected-3 state. Undo has not reliably restored the pre-overfill state.
Current recovery/replay idea: treat the board as restarted from an early-cycle layout. From a clean-looking state, begin with select, then use up as the strongest early trigger of meaningful changes; avoid overfilling the bottom 3/11 bar later.
Step 63-70 replay note: replayed from a clean-like state with select, then up, then select, then down. This appears to recreate the earlier redistributed state from which select was previously the next continuation move.
Step 75-76: repeated selects seem to continue the reduction phase without a new promotion.
Step 79-80: replay appears to have reproduced the earlier top 3+8+1+5 state after converting 4 -> 1. Select then restored the stable top-composite state.
Step 81-103: stable top-composite state appears recovered again. Critical danger: one extra right near the end overfills the bar and resets the board back near the early selected-3 state. This has happened repeatedly, so when only a tiny 11 remnant remains, stop using right blindly and reassess.
Current replay status: another overfill reset occurred around step 110. Replay path again followed up -> select -> down. Repeated selects from the redistributed state continue changing the left-side source stacks while the top remains pure 5.
Step 128-134: attempted up from a candidate pure-4-like redistributed state did not yield the expected 4->1 conversion, so resume select-driven cycling from redistributed states until recovery.
Step 139 correction: despite the large remaining 11-bar, the main grid was not yet the final stable composite; it showed top 3+8+1+5 with lower-left 1+8+3+4. From this pre-final state, select restored the stable top composite 3+8+1+4 again. Resume right-based bar advancement, but stop and reassess once the visible 11 remnant becomes tiny.
Step 143-158: stable top composite appears restored again, and right-based bar advancement eventually reached the 1-cell 11 stub. Both right and select from the tiniest stub reset the board back near the early selected-3/pure-5 layout, so the level is not safely finished by either of those endpoint actions.
